sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the innovation of the manna from heaven over bread from the earth is that it reveals the level of "all that comes from the mouth of Hashem," which is above both immanent and transcendent Divine presence, and this was made into blood and flesh.

translations.translation: And this is [the meaning of] "And He fed you the manna... to make known to you that not by bread alone does man live, but by all that comes from the mouth of Hashem does man live."
Through this, the innovation of bread from heaven over bread from the earth is understood, even as the bread from the earth is at its most elevated level
(and as mentioned above, even bread from the earth in spiritual terms is a lofty matter).
For the assumption that man lives by bread alone is analogous to what is said, that the entirety of creation is in a manner of "olam" (world), from the term "helem" (concealment) and hiding,
even though the world was created in its fullness.
This is because there only the aspect of "Memaleh Kol Almin" (Immanent) is revealed
(in the language of the Zohar and Kabbalah).
And about this it is said that the ultimate perfection of the Jewish people is to know that not by bread alone does man live, but by all that comes from the mouth of Hashem does man live,
for "motza" (comes from) is a term meaning source and root, as explained in many places,
for relative to the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin, this is the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin (Transcendent),
and in a more general sense, it is the aspect that is above both Memaleh and Sovev,
above the entire order of Hishtalshelus (the chain of descent),
which is like the matter of dew, for dew is never withheld.
And so that this knowledge should be,
therefore "He fed you the manna,"
for this matter
(of bread from heaven,
the "motza" of the mouth of Hashem)
became blood and flesh like his flesh,
meaning that it permeated even the blood and flesh.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that even prior revelations through "bread from the earth" were within the realm of Memaleh Kol Almin, whereas the manna was a preparation for receiving the Torah in a manner of "walking" that transcends all order.

translations.translation: And this is the innovation of bread from heaven,
for even though before this there was the aspect of bread from the earth,
and through it there were lofty and wondrous revelations,
and as mentioned above, "a child does not know how to call 'Abba' until he tastes the taste of grain,"
and even that the aspect of bread from the earth brought about
(the aspect of knowing how to call "Abba")
that they already said "This is my G-d and I will glorify Him,"
nevertheless, all this can be
(only)
in the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin.
For even though at that moment there was the aspect of the revelation of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory and He Himself redeemed them,
and likewise at the Splitting of the Sea there was a revelation loftier than the prophecy of the greatest of prophets,
nevertheless, this was only for a moment,
but afterward the service was
(ordered)
day by day and level after level,
which proves that this belongs to Memaleh Kol Almin,
which comes in order and Hishtalshelus.
Therefore, when they needed to receive the Torah, and in such a manner that through the Giving of the Torah something new was created
(meaning a level higher than the aspect of Torah that existed before,
for they fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given),
which is the aspect of the Torah specifically as it is in the manner of "walking" (halichah),
for the true meaning of "walking" is without limit,
even to the level of Ein Sof,

and even to such a level that even when one has already reached the limit of the Torah, that is a boundary relative to the aspect of Torah that must be reached through the fulfillment of the commandment
(which is also a giving of power)
of "ascending in holiness,"
as a preparation for this, it was necessary to have "Behold I will rain down for you bread from heaven,"
which is above Memaleh Kol Almin, etc.
Therefore, even though they were already at a lofty level as mentioned,
and were in a state called "your going after Me in the desert, in a land not sown,"
nevertheless, this is specifically called "your going after Me,"
which is not an aspect of pnimiyus (internality), as explained at length in the preceding maamarim,
and even the entire service during the time of exile,
and moreover the entire service in the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, all is in the externality of Atik,
and specifically in the future will the aspect of the pnimiyus (internality) of Atik be revealed.
And since this is the externality of Atik
(called "your going after Me,"
because)
it is not the true aspect of "face" (panim),
and the true aspect of "face" in the Torah is in a manner where there is no existence of "back" (achor) at all,
like the Tablets, which had no front and back
(but were entirely face),
as explained above
at length,
which is the aspect of the "song" in the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the manna, which had no waste and is above the entire order of Hishtalshelus, was eaten and became blood and flesh, thereby elevating the people to the level of "walking in the Torah."

translations.translation: And this is "Behold I will rain down... in order that I may test them, whether they will walk in My Torah."
For in order to come to the aspect of "walking" in the Torah,
the aspect of the manna must precede it,
and as the Mechilta states,
"The Torah was only given to the eaters of the manna,"
and the precise wording is "to the eaters of the manna"
(and as explained above in the interpretation of "And He fed you the manna"),
that the manna must be in a manner that it becomes blood and flesh like his flesh.
For the aspect of the manna is that it had no waste,
being entirely above the order of Hishtalshelus,
since it is above Memaleh Kol Almin and Sovev Kol Almin, and also above the third level
(that is above Memaleh and Sovev).
And through this aspect coming in a manner of eating and becoming blood and flesh like his flesh,
through this the aspect of "anesenu" (I will test them) is brought about,
for
[as explained in many discourses
and also in the lexicons,
"anesenu" is an aspect of raising and lifting, like "I will lift up a banner" (erom nisi),
for through eating the manna they are elevated above the entire order of Hishtalshelus, through which they come to the aspect of "walking" in the Torah.
And this is
what is written,
"an omer per skull" specifically,
for the aspect of the "skull" (gulgoleth) is above even the head,
and as it is written,
"Lift up the head of all the congregation of the children of Israel... by their skulls,"
meaning
that the lifting of the head
("Lift up the head")
is to their skulls, which are above the head,
and this was also the aspect of the manna, which was specifically an omer per skull,
for its purpose is to effect in Israel the knowledge that "not by bread alone
(Memaleh Kol Almin)
does man live, but by all that comes from the mouth of Hashem does man live,"
as explained above.
